card.does: Stores electricity in one cell and gives it to the parts you wire to it.
card.gives: Gives: power (red) from one AA cell, with half the push of a 2-cell battery pack.
card.needs: Needs: power lines (red) in a loop from plus, through a part, back to minus.
card.popularMechanics: A single AA cell like this keeps a wall clock ticking for months.
card.safetyNote: Use real battery packs only with an adult nearby, and never join plus straight to minus.

failureModes.cardLine: Short circuit: the battery pack drains fast.
failureModes.hint: This battery pack is in a loop with nothing in it that uses power
failureModes.teachingNote: When plus is joined back to minus with nothing that uses power in between, such as a bare wire, a closed switch or a different battery pack side by side, nothing holds the current back, so the pack empties in seconds and grows warm.

failureModes.cardLine: No loop: nothing on the battery pack works.
failureModes.hint: This battery pack has no loop back to minus
failureModes.teachingNote: A battery pack gives power only round a closed loop from plus back to minus. With no loop at all, nothing flows and nothing wired to it works.
